ARCANE - Incidence Calibration and Seeding Analysis

Novel pathogen introduction on the French inter-hospital transfer network

MESuRS/Cnam - Task 4.3

September 2026

Methodology

Study population and network

The French inter-hospital transfer network was derived from 2024 PMSI (Programme de Medicalisation des Systemes d’Information) administrative discharge data. The network comprises 2,529 hospitals (etablissements de soins) including acute care (MCO - Medecine, Chirurgie, Obstetrique), rehabilitation (SSR - Soins de Suite et de Readaptation), psychiatric (PSY), home hospitalisation (HAD - Hospitalisation a Domicile), and mixed (MCO/SSR) facilities. Daily transfer counts between each pair of facilities were derived from rolling 7-day sums, divided by 7 to give daily averages and rounded to the nearest integer (minimum 1). Total network beds: 374,545.

Patient flow model

The model assumes constant full bed occupancy throughout the simulation. Daily patient turnover at each hospital is determined by observed daily admission counts from the 2024 PMSI (NO_ADMISSION_DAILY_DIRCT_HBN dataset; 0hospital-days). Because occupancy is assumed constant, daily discharges equal daily admissions at each facility. The pathogen transmission status of discharging patients is determined by a hypergeometric draw - sampling without replacement from the current colonised (I) and susceptible (S) patients at each facility - preserving the colonisation proportion among those leaving. Of discharged patients, a facility-specific fraction is transferred to other hospitals (via the transfer probability matrix P); the remainder are admitted from the community. The number of patients admitted from the community equals total admissions minus transfers received. If incoming transfers exceed a facility’s admission quota on a given day, excess transfers are scaled down proportionally (capacity enforcement). Community-admitted patients may be colonised at admission with probability pi (pi_vec).

SIS transmission model

Within each hospital h on each day t, susceptible patients (S) can acquire colonisation from infected/colonised patients (I) according to a frequency-dependent stochastic SIS (Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible) process:

P(new colonisation | S, I, N) = 1 − exp(−beta x I/N)

where beta (beta) is the daily within-hospital transmission probability per susceptible-infectious contact (units: per day), N = S + I is total hospital occupancy, and new_inf ~ Binomial(S, p_inf). Biological decolonisation occurs at rate gamma (gamma) = 1/387 per day, corresponding to a mean carriage duration of 387 days for ESBL-producing Enterobacterales (ESBL-E). No patient isolation (alpha = 0) is assumed.

Incidence calibration

Incidence targets were derived from ECDC EARS-Net 2022 antibiotic resistance carriage prevalence benchmarks, converted to hospital-acquired incidence per 1,000 patient-days using:

incidence = (gamma + 1/LOS) x (P_total − pi) x 1,000

where LOS is the network-weighted mean length of stay (9.28 days from PMSI data) and P_total is the ECDC carriage prevalence for each resistance tier. Three tiers are defined using ECDC official category boundaries:

Incidence calibration targets derived from ECDC EARS-Net 2022. CRE = Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales. VRE = Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci. MRSA = Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus. ESBL-E = Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase-producing Enterobacterales. pd = patient-days.
Tier ECDC category ECDC carriage range Incidence target (/1,000 pd) Epidemiological examples
Low low (>1-10%) 1-10% 0.99-10.92 CRE in France/Germany, VRE in Scandinavia, MRSA in low-burden Northern Europe
Moderate moderate (>10-20%) 10-20% 10.92-21.96 MRSA in moderate-burden settings, ESBL-E in Eastern EU
High high (>20-50%) 20-50% 21.96-55.06 MRSA in Southern/Eastern Europe (Greece, Romania), ESBL-E in high-burden settings

beta was calibrated via grid search (beta = 0.005-0.120, step 0.005; 24 values) combined with three community carriage scenarios (pi = 0.001, 0.010, 0.050), run across 10 parallel cluster jobs (3 replicates per job = 30 total replicates per beta x pi combination). The best-fit beta per tier was defined as the replicate whose achieved incidence was closest to the tier midpoint.

Seeding simulation

Seeding rules - eight candidate introduction hospitals were evaluated:

Seeding rules. NC = Network-central. FTR = Facility-type random. MCO = Medecine Chirurgie Obstetrique (acute care). SSR = Soins de Suite et de Readaptation (rehabilitation). MCO/SSR = mixed facility. All centrality metrics computed on the directed transfer network using igraph (betweenness: directed, unnormalised).
Seed rule Type Selection criterion
Network hub (NC) Network-central (NC) Hospital ranking first on ALL five centrality metrics simultaneously: in-degree, out-degree, betweenness centrality, total bed count, and outgoing transfer volume. In this network, all five metrics identified the same facility (750100125, MCO/SSR, Ile-de-France, 1,713 beds), consistent with a scale-free network structure.
Random MCO (FTR) Facility-type random (FTR) One acute care hospital (MCO) drawn uniformly at random per simulation replicate.
Random SSR (FTR) Facility-type random (FTR) One rehabilitation hospital (SSR) drawn uniformly at random per simulation replicate.
Random MCO/SSR (FTR) Facility-type random (FTR) One mixed acute/rehabilitation facility (MCO/SSR) drawn uniformly at random per simulation replicate.

Simulation parameters:

Seeding simulation parameters. SS = steady state.
Parameter Value Description
N_SEED_INF 5 Index cases introduced on day 0 in the seed hospital
Tmax 732 days Simulation duration (2 x 366 days, cycling 2024 PMSI data annually)
gamma (gamma) 1/387 per day Daily biological decolonisation rate; mean carriage ~387 days (ESBL-E)
pi_vec (pi) 0 Community carriage on admission - novel pathogen assumption (no external reservoir)
N_REP 10 per job x 10 jobs = 100 total Replicates per (seed rule x tier) combination
SS_WINDOW 30 days Last N days used to compute steady-state (SS) incidence metrics
Beta draws Truncated normal (mean=mean_beta, sd from 95% CI width) Per-hospital beta drawn independently; propagates calibration uncertainty

Outcome metric definitions

All outcomes are computed per simulation replicate. Analyses use non-extinct replicates only unless stated otherwise.

Primary outcome metric definitions. I_loc = infected (colonised) patients per hospital. N_t = total occupied beds on day t. new_inf_t = new colonisations on day t. SS = steady state. pd = patient-days. HAI = healthcare-associated infection.
Metric Abbreviation Scale Exact formula Time window Interpretation
Network steady-state incidence net_ss_inc National (bed-weighted) mean[sum(new_inf_t)/sum(N_t) x 1,000] over last SS_WINDOW days Last 30 days National hospital-acquired incidence rate per 1,000 patient-days at near-endemic equilibrium. Directly comparable to SPARES and ECDC HAI surveillance.
Facility-level mean steady-state incidence fac_ss_inc_mean Facility (unweighted) mean over active hospitals of [new_inf_t[h]/N_t[h] x 1,000], then mean over last 30 days Last 30 days Mean of per-hospital daily acquisition rates, giving equal weight to each facility regardless of size. Closer to facility-level HAI reporting.
Network cumulative incidence net_cumul_inc National (bed-weighted) mean[sum(new_inf_t)/sum(N_t) x 1,000] over all Tmax days All 732 days Mean daily acquisition rate over the entire simulation. Reflects the integrated burden of colonisation throughout the epidemic trajectory, not just the end state.
Network steady-state prevalence net_ss_prev_pct National (bed-weighted) mean[sum(I_loc_t)/total_beds x 100] over last 30 days Last 30 days Proportion of total network beds occupied by colonised patients at near-endemic equilibrium. NOTE: values above 100% indicate a simulation capacity overflow bug and are capped at 100% in all displays.
Facility-level mean steady-state prevalence fac_ss_prev_mean_pct Facility (unweighted) mean over hospitals of [I_loc_t[h]/beds[h] x 100], then mean over last 30 days Last 30 days Mean of per-hospital colonisation proportions. Unweighted: a 10-bed rural facility counts the same as a 1,000-bed university hospital.
Extinction ever_extinct
sum(I_loc) == 0 at any point during the simulation Any day 1-732 Pathogen died out - no colonised patients remain. With pi=0 (novel pathogen), extinction occurs when the pathogen fails to establish through transfers and within-hospital transmission alone.
Steady-state reached ss_reached
0.9 <= net_ss_inc / net_cumul_inc <= 1.1 Ratio of last-30d mean to overall mean The epidemic has stabilised: the last 30-day incidence is within 10% of the overall mean. Ratio > 1.1 = still growing; ratio < 0.9 = declining.

Results compilation

Local (PSOCK, Windows) and cluster (FORK, Linux) simulation results were compiled by compile_seeding_novel.R. Each source is loaded separately, tagged with a source label, and row-bound into a single sim_summary data frame. Each simulation replicate receives a globally unique identifier (global_sim_id) to prevent collision between local and cluster job indices. The compiled file saved to Outputs/seeding_novel/compiled/ is the single input to this report.
